claims.paper_title: Journal of Materials Chemistry A
claims.component: phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted / protonated phosphate network)
claims.claim_text: Phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted network) provides an amorphous, continuous proton-transport medium (D1) with OH-enabled hydrogen-bonded proton mobility (D6) and strong immobilisation/retention within a rigid network (D7), with stability reported up to 280 °C (manual_26f0dcfc01).

Phosphate glass provides a dense hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor landscape (D6): protons are described as forming much stronger hydrogen bonds in phosphate glasses than in silicate glasses (manual_3d7d6d5d7b).

Phosphate glass provides only conditionally retained conducting phase (D7): the long-term stability of proton conductivity is described as problematic and dependent on maintaining high humidity (manual_3d7d6d5d7b).

claims.claim_text: Deep eutectic solvent (DES) provides a putatively non-crystallising acid-like proton-carrier environment (D4): the membrane’s proton conduction improves upon DES incorporation alongside altered thermal behaviour, consistent with eutectic-mediated suppression of crystallisation relative to neat phases (manual_42051140ac).
